assessment_status: Research synthesis by an AI agent; no independent licensed legal review

study.title: AI-Powered Lawyering: AI Reasoning Models, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and the Future of Legal Practice
study.population: Upper-level and LL.M. students at Michigan and Minnesota
study.assignment: Randomized stable groups; each participant two tasks per condition
study.assessment: Three coauthors with practice experience; treatment/identity-blind; five 1–7 quality attributes; hallucination indicator
study.productivity_definition: Sum of quality scores divided by fraction of allotted time used

NDA.interpretation: No statistically significant speed, quality, or productivity improvement

limits: No autonomous-agent, commercial-price, professional-acceptance or operating-surplus test
study.license: CC BY-NC 4.0; cite findings, do not redistribute paper as a commercial product

professional_boundary.intended_professional_user: An Ontario-qualified commercial lawyer or supervised legal team

statute.summary: Applying legal principles and judgment to a person's circumstances can constitute legal services; practice and provision are restricted to licensees, subject to authorized exceptions. A support label alone does not determine legal characterization.
statute.retrieval_limit: Government page direct retrieval returned 403; current primary indexed excerpts verified definitions and section 26.1 restriction, not full consolidated exceptions.

LSO_guidance.summary: Relevant obligations are competence, confidentiality, honesty/candour, supervision, reasonable fees and candour to tribunals. AI output relied upon must be independently verified by a human. Professional judgment remains with the licensee. Confidential material requires appropriate safeguards; this study uses no such material. Disclosure depends on the use and its implications. Tool costs passed through as disbursements must be actual, reasonable and disclosed.

LSO_white_paper.summary: Licensees retain responsibility for AI-assisted work and must exercise active expert independent judgment. The professional may delegate appropriate tasks but cannot replace necessary professional competence with a tool.

professional_boundary.freshness_note: Primary LSO resource listing still presents the April 2024 guidance at the check date. A May 2026 A2I consultation is not authorization for this provider. No regulatory approval or comprehensive legal opinion is claimed.
